label: sparse token-conjunction feature, late copy phase (e.g. input a after 3)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.018% of steps). It never fires at t<3 and is almost never active on the delimiter step. About 76% of its mass is in the copy phase, rising toward the final outputs (to_go 0-2 holds about 82% of the mass, lift up to 11x at t=17). The other 24% is in the original phase at t=3-5, often in sequences that start f s k. It is enriched for input tokens a/r/i/u/q, previous tokens 3/k/e/z/j and output tokens 0/f/x/c/d/i. The strongest pattern is a copy-phase input a right after 3 (the top example is 3 l t b 3 [a]). Even so, each of these cues has low precision: most 3->a bigrams late in the copy phase do not fire it, and conjunctions of the token sets reach F1 of at most about 0.16. Magnitude is nearly flat (median 0.117, max 0.204), and no variable that modulates it was found. It looks like a specific multi-token hidden-state conjunction that the per-step variables cannot capture.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=3 & prev_tok=k (+5.79), phase=2 & in_tok=i (+4.55), in_tok=r (+4.29), phase=2 & out_tok=f (+4.04), prev_tok=3 (+3.93), phase=2 & in_tok=h (+3.73). Lower it: t=9 (-2.90), prev3_tok=- (-2.85), t=8 (-2.82), prev_tok=<DEL> (-2.50).
